content.value_statement: Test planning can drift when teams manage test types separately. This skill organizes coverage goals, quality gates, execution flow, and reporting.
actual_capabilities: Defines test plans and coverage goals for project components.
Coordinates unit, integration, E2E, performance, and security testing.
Packages testing context for specialized test skills.
Tracks quality gates, failures, flaky tests, and coverage metrics.
Documents event formats for test-related status updates.
Lists testing standards, data practices, and common test patterns.
limitations: It provides orchestration guidance, not a standalone test runner.
It references companion test skills that may not exist in every workspace.
It does not include framework-specific commands for each language.
It depends on project context to choose realistic coverage targets.

use_cases.title: Plan Release Testing
use_cases.description: Create a test plan that maps changed components to required test types, coverage goals, and quality gates.

use_cases.title: Improve Coverage
use_cases.description: Identify gaps in unit, integration, and E2E coverage before a feature reaches review.

use_cases.title: Standardize CI Checks
use_cases.description: Define pass criteria, failure handling, and reporting expectations for automated test pipelines.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Test Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a test plan for [component]. Include unit, integration, and E2E coverage goals.

prompt_templates.title: Review Current Coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the current tests for [feature]. Identify missing scenarios, weak assertions, and coverage risks.

prompt_templates.title: Define Quality Gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Define quality gates for [release]. Include coverage thresholds, failure policies, performance checks, and security testing.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Multi-Skill Testing
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced orchestration across specialized test skills
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a testing coordination plan for [project change]. Assign work across unit, integration, E2E, performance, and security testing.

output_examples.input: Plan tests for an authentication change.
output_examples.output: A test plan covering public method unit tests, database integration checks, login and password reset E2E flows, performance targets, and security validation.

output_examples.input: Assess whether a feature is ready for CI gating.
output_examples.output: A readiness summary with required coverage, failing test review, flaky test handling, retry policy, and release-blocking conditions.

output_examples.input: Coordinate testing after a user-service update.
output_examples.output: A task breakdown for specialized test skills, expected status events, result reporting needs, and quality metrics to track.

best_practices: Provide the changed component, affected workflows, and current test coverage before asking for a plan.
Use the skill to define pass criteria before implementation work begins.
Review flaky tests and slow suites as release risks, not only maintenance issues.
anti_patterns: Using one test type as a substitute for complete quality coverage.
Setting coverage thresholds without reviewing important user workflows.
Ignoring test failures because retry logic eventually passes.

faq.question: Does this skill run tests directly?
faq.answer: No. It coordinates testing strategy, expected checks, quality gates, and reporting workflows.

faq.question: Which test types does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers unit, integration, E2E, performance, and security testing at a planning level.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Does it require companion skills?
faq.answer: It can reference companion test skills, but users can also apply the guidance manually.

faq.question: What coverage target does it recommend?
faq.answer: The skill uses an 80 percent minimum coverage goal and asks for critical paths to be covered.

faq.question: Is it framework specific?
faq.answer: No. It provides general testing orchestration patterns rather than framework-specific implementation commands.
